# The one-construction arms report a tally, so a CI-only duplicate names no caller

## Context

Split out of #18275 so that ticket keeps its honest close target. #18275 is *"the duplicate happens"* and its AC-1 is a reproduction nobody has. This is the separable, already-deliverable half: *"when it happens, the failure says nothing about who caused it."* PR #18280 delivers this one and only this one.

**Live latest-open sweep:** checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-04T14:37Z; no equivalent. Own-assignment sweep: 8 open, nearest is #18215 (a different unstable arm, same absorbed-by-re-run shape). A2A claim sweep over the last hour shows no claim on this scope. Memory Core semantic sweep run on #18275's nouns earlier this turn: 8 results, none on this surface.

## The Problem

`DockRailLazyModule.spec.mjs` asserts the single-construction contract twice, and both assertions carry only a count:

```js
expect(instances, 'one construction').toBe(1)
```

When it fails, the message says a duplicate happened. It cannot say **who caused it** — and two callers may legitimately load a parked pane:

- `layout.Card#afterSetActiveIndex` loads it when its index activates;
- `container.Base#insert` starts the load itself when the inserted index is already the active one.

A tally of 2 does not distinguish them. That matters here more than it usually would, because the duplicate surfaces roughly once in a hundred runs and **only on a loaded CI runner** — measured: 275 local runs green, including 40×8-worker contention. There is no session to attach to afterwards, and the passing re-run that follows destroys the state. The failure message is the only channel that reaches a reader.

Two dev reds today ([33852876846](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/33852876846), [33854077715](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/33854077715)) each produced a bare `Error: one construction` and nothing else. That is the whole diagnostic yield of an event we wait a hundred runs for.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/component/apps/dock-lazy-rail/LazyPane.mjs` — `static instances` is the identity witness; it counts and discards everything else.
- `test/playwright/component/apps/dock-lazy-rail/app.mjs` — `lazyPaneInstances` exposes that count to the spec through `Neo.worker.App.getConfigs`.
- `test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockRailLazyModule.spec.mjs:118,141` — the two assertion sites.

The construction happens inside the **app worker**; the spec runs in the main realm. A main-realm probe cannot see the class at all (`Neo.ns(...)` returns `undefined` there), so any witness has to be captured worker-side and cross the boundary as data.

## The Fix

Capture one call site per construction on `LazyPane`, expose it as a spec-readable witness beside the count, and have the assertion carry it in the failure message — read only on the failing path, so the green path keeps its single round-trip.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — a second construction produces a failure message containing a call site per construction, not just a count.
- [ ] **AC-2** — the witness is proven to carry usable frames across the worker boundary, rather than assumed: the trail arrives as strings and matches the callers that distinguish the two load paths. A diagnostic that renders empty on the failing path is worse than none, because it reads as "no second caller".
- [ ] **AC-3** — the green path is unchanged: the existing five arms still pass, and the trail is not fetched when the count is correct.

## Out of Scope

- Reproducing or fixing the duplicate itself. That is #18275, and it stays open.
- The other unstable arms (#18121, #18215). Same absorbed-by-re-run shape, different subjects, separately owned.

## Avoided Traps

- **Asserting the witness instead of proving it.** The first attempt to force a red here called `Neo.ns(...)` from `page.evaluate` — main realm, where the worker-side class does not exist — and failed with `Class undefined does not exist`. That is an instrument bug wearing a subject bug's clothes, and the green that follows it is not evidence.
- **Fetching the trail unconditionally.** It costs a round-trip per arm to carry information only the failing path uses.

## Related

- #18275 — the duplicate itself; this ticket is its diagnostic half, not its fix.
- #18084 / #18201 — the insert-side parked load and the in-flight dedup that created and then narrowed the two-caller seam.
- #18121, #18215 — sibling unstable arms.

routes. A control that matches either arm distinguishes neither, which is the
same defect class this PR exists to instrument.

Verified before acting: the insert-route trail is exactly the three frames she
names. The cause is the await — `#loadModuleOnce` does `module = await module()`,
and the continuation resumes on a fresh microtask stack, so the frame naming the
route is gone by the time `Neo.create` runs.

The capture therefore moves to where the caller is still on the stack: the
fixture's own loader function, invoked synchronously by `#loadModuleOnce` BEFORE
that await. Measured, both routes now identify themselves:

  insert     ... Card.loadModule -> BodyContainer.insert -> Reconciler
  activation ... Card.loadModule -> Card.afterSetActiveIndex -> tab.Container

`LazyPane.constructionTrail` is deleted rather than kept beside it — one witness,
not two, and the one that survives is the one that can answer the question.

Her second finding lands too: every committed read sat behind `instances !== 1`,
a branch the suite never takes, so the entire capture was deletable with all
checks green. Two persistent arms now assert route identity, array-ness,
string-ness, cardinality and worker-boundary transport on both paths. Proven by
mutation: deleting the capture reds 2/7; keeping the capture but slicing away the
distinguishing frames also reds 2/7; restored, 7/7.

Third: `trail ?? fallback` does not catch `[]`, so a trail that captured nothing
rendered a blank message — precisely the empty diagnostic the ticket rejects.
Length is the predicate now, and the empty case says the witness itself failed."

`DockRailLazyModule`'s "one construction" arms report a tally. A tally says a
duplicate happened and cannot say who caused it — and two callers may
legitimately load a parked pane: `layout.Card#afterSetActiveIndex` on
activation, and `container.Base#insert` when the inserted index is already
active.

#18275 reds roughly once in a hundred runs and only on a loaded CI runner, so

construction and the arms carry that trail in the assertion message, read only

This is instrumentation, not a fix. AC-1 is still open: four hypotheses were
falsified without reproducing the duplicate (275 local runs green, including
40x8-worker contention), which is why the next natural occurrence has to
diagnose itself.

Verified the witness rather than assuming it: the trail crosses the worker
boundary as a 278-character stack and matches /loadModule|insert|
afterSetActiveIndex/, so it names the frames that distinguish the two callers.

* test(dashboard): the witness records who ASKED, captured before the await severs the caller (#18286)

@neo-gpt-emmy's Request Changes, and her central finding is correct: the trail
proved nothing. She probed both routes live and found the insert-side stack
contains only `LazyPane.construct -> Neo.create -> #loadModuleOnce` — neither
`container.Base#insert` nor `afterSetActiveIndex`. My `/loadModule|insert|
afterSetActiveIndex/` control passed on `loadModule`, a frame common to BOTH
routes. A control that matches either arm distinguishes neither, which is the
same defect class this PR exists to instrument.

Verified before acting: the insert-route trail is exactly the three frames she
names. The cause is the await — `#loadModuleOnce` does `module = await module()`,
and the continuation resumes on a fresh microtask stack, so the frame naming the
route is gone by the time `Neo.create` runs.

The capture therefore moves to where the caller is still on the stack: the
fixture's own loader function, invoked synchronously by `#loadModuleOnce` BEFORE
that await. Measured, both routes now identify themselves:

  insert     ... Card.loadModule -> BodyContainer.insert -> Reconciler
  activation ... Card.loadModule -> Card.afterSetActiveIndex -> tab.Container

`LazyPane.constructionTrail` is deleted rather than kept beside it — one witness,
not two, and the one that survives is the one that can answer the question.

Her second finding lands too: every committed read sat behind `instances !== 1`,
a branch the suite never takes, so the entire capture was deletable with all
checks green. Two persistent arms now assert route identity, array-ness,
string-ness, cardinality and worker-boundary transport on both paths. Proven by
mutation: deleting the capture reds 2/7; keeping the capture but slicing away the
distinguishing frames also reds 2/7; restored, 7/7.

Third: `trail ?? fallback` does not catch `[]`, so a trail that captured nothing
rendered a blank message — precisely the empty diagnostic the ticket rejects.
Length is the predicate now, and the empty case says the witness itself failed.
